o1.biggest_strength: It correctly treats the Instagram/Facebook in-app checkout issue as a ship-now bug, sizes the upside at about ₹34 lakh gross margin per month, and ranks tests around the real customer blockers.
o1.biggest_mistake: It applies one broad 4-week, all-traffic, 10% order-lift testing rule too evenly, instead of tailoring sample size and main metric more clearly for mobile-only or top-of-page tests.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give each test its own explicit traffic scope, duration and detectable effect, especially for mobile-only size and hero tests, while keeping the bug fix first.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads the browser split correctly, calls the in-app checkout bug a no-test fix with the money attached, and gives each ranked test a clear metric, guardrail, split, runtime and MDE.
o2.biggest_mistake: It leaves a few implementation blanks such as EMI amount and firmness rating, and Test 5 partly overlaps with the ship-now reviews change.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the remaining placeholders by wording them as dynamic values from the product/payment systems and separate the already-shipped review summary from the hero-image test.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 2 is a little easier to run tomorrow because it shows the funnel cuts, mobile-specific test sizing, and per-test split/duration/MDE more plainly. Output 1 is very good, but its one-size-fits-all test sizing needs a bit more owner rework.
